subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-streamed deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should the permanent block-streaming contract require explicit seam metadata or another complete in-budget boundary mechanism before landing, or may maintainers accept this partial text-only repair for common cases?
rationale: The bug and shared code boundary are clear, but the remaining near-maxChars case requires a maintainer choice about the streaming payload contract and whether partial improvement is acceptable.

options.title: Require complete seam handling
options.body: Ask for one consolidated fix that preserves paragraph boundaries across both in-budget and near-maxChars splits before merge.

options.title: Adopt explicit boundary metadata
options.body: Carry paragraph/newline/hard-split seam semantics through chunker, subscriber, and coalescer if text-only chunks cannot satisfy all invariants.

options.title: Accept partial repair
options.body: Land the common-case text-only improvement while leaving the near-limit boundary documented as remaining work on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Require complete seam handling
recommendation.body: Ask for one consolidated fix that preserves paragraph boundaries across both in-budget and near-maxChars splits before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest history across coalescing, chunking hardening, and streaming docs for the affected boundary.
